entries.title: Portal
entries.definitive_edition: Portal with RTX for the main campaign, plus Still Alive bonus chambers as secondary content

emulation.notes: Use native Windows. Xbox 360 emulation is unnecessary if Switch Companion Collection or original hardware covers the Still Alive chambers.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows Portal with RTX on RTX-capable hardware

primary.why: The original game shipped first in The Orange Box and later reached Mac, Linux, Android, and Switch. For the main campaign, Portal with RTX is the highest-fidelity Windows route because it is a free Portal-owner DLC with full ray tracing, DLSS, high-resolution physically based textures, and enhanced models. The Switch Companion Collection is tracked separately for the Still Alive bonus chambers.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows version with Portal with RTX on RTX-capable hardware for the main campaign. Keep the original Steam build installed as a fallback for compatibility, and use the Switch Companion Collection or Xbox 360 Still Alive only to check the bonus chambers.

secondary.exclusive_content: Portal: Still Alive bonus chambers included in Portal: Companion Collection.
secondary.what_to_play: Play only the Still Alive bonus chambers if they are not available in the chosen Windows/RTX route.
secondary.why: The Switch port includes additional levels from Portal: Still Alive, while the Windows primary is chosen for ray-traced fidelity.

secondary.what_to_play: Use Portal: Still Alive only as a fallback source for those bonus chambers if Switch access is unavailable.
secondary.why: The Still Alive release is the source of the bonus chamber set; it is not the best main-campaign fidelity route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows Portal with RTX is the fidelity pick for the main campaign, while the Switch Companion Collection and Xbox 360 Still Alive route are tracked for the Still Alive bonus chambers. entries.remaster_caveats: Portal with RTX requires RTX-capable hardware and is a visual remaster path, so keep the original Steam build as a compatibility fallback. The Switch collection is valuable for Still Alive bonus chambers but is not the top-fidelity route.

entries.title: Portal 2

emulation.notes: Use native Windows. Console emulation is unnecessary unless preserving a specific console release is the goal.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native Windows with current Steam build and tested video settings

primary.why: Portal 2 launched on Windows, Mac, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360, later reached Linux, and was released on Switch through Portal: Companion Collection. The Windows Steam version is the highest-fidelity and most expandable route, with continued PC updates, Vulkan support, and Workshop-related fixes.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows build, enable the best tested video settings for the capture PC, and use the official Steam route for co-op and Workshop/community chambers. Use console versions only for ownership or comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Native PC Steam route with the best resolution/settings ceiling, Workshop ecosystem, and ongoing update path.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most complete practical route for campaign, co-op, and community content.

all_releases.fidelity: Native Mac Steam route.
all_releases.reason: skip: same core game, but Windows has the stronger current settings/capture and compatibility route.

all_releases.reason: skip: useful native route, but Windows remains the default archive capture target unless Linux/Steam Deck is the intended setup.

all_releases.fidelity: Portable console route bundled with Portal.
all_releases.reason: skip: convenient portable route, but no sourced exclusive Portal 2 story content over Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Windows Steam route is both the fidelity pick and the route with the broadest official community-content ecosystem; no sourced console-exclusive campaign content is logged.

entries.remaster_caveats: No separate remaster replaces the Windows primary as of this pass. The Switch collection is a convenient bundle, not a fidelity upgrade over PC.

entries.title: Bridge Constructor Portal

emulation.notes: Native PC build; mobile/console releases are control-preference alternatives.

primary.why: Bridge Constructor Portal is a licensed Bridge Constructor and Portal crossover released on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows, Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. The Windows PC route has the highest settings/capture ceiling and has active community compatibility tracking.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows build for the main run. Use mobile or console versions only if testing platform-specific controls, since there is no exclusive story or level content outside PC.

entries.title: Aperture Desk Job

emulation.notes: Native Steam build. A controller is required for the Windows route.

primary.why: Aperture Desk Job is a free Portal-series game/tech demo for Linux and Windows, built to showcase Steam Deck controls while also playable on Windows with a controller. Windows is the highest-fidelity capture route when using a desktop GPU and controller.
primary.how_to_play: Use the free Steam Windows build with a controller. Use Steam Deck/Linux only when documenting the intended hardware experience.

all_releases.fidelity: Steam Deck-targeted Linux route and intended hardware showcase.
all_releases.reason: skip: intended-device route, but not a higher-fidelity capture route than Windows PC.

all_releases.fidelity: Native Windows route with desktop capture/GPU ceiling; controller required for play.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity capture route while preserving the full playable content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Steam Deck is the intended showcase device, but no sourced content is exclusive to Linux/SteamOS; Windows is the capture-fidelity pick.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a short free Steam Deck showcase game rather than Portal 3; preserve that context in display text.
